themes.title: Quantum Communication & Networks
themes.tagline: Reliable and private communication over lossy, correlated and adversarial quantum links.
themes.problem: Quantum networks must carry information over lossy channels whose noise is correlated across modes, in the presence of active adversaries, and for applications that care about meaning rather than raw bits. How much can multi-mode (MIMO) quantum links deliver when losses are correlated? Can communication be anonymous and full-duplex against an adversary? What does a semantic, task-level view of quantum communication look like for industrial networks?
themes.approach: I study MIMO quantum communication over correlated pure-loss channels; controlled quantum semantic communication for industrial cyber-physical systems (CPS) networks; full-duplex anonymous communication in adversarial quantum networks; quantum random access codes for image transmission; and quantum fusion learning for 6G networks. This line is tied to the NRF programmes on integrating 6G wireless with quantum networks and on meta-privacy.

themes.title: Quantum Control & Hardware
themes.tagline: Learning-based pulse and Hamiltonian control for Rydberg, single-photon and superconducting platforms.
themes.problem: Gate and state-preparation fidelity on real hardware is limited by pulse design and by how well control and device physics are co-designed. Can reinforcement learning and reservoir-style learning find pulses and Hamiltonian controls that hand-designed protocols miss, and can circuit-level design (such as Purcell filtering) be made analytical rather than trial-and-error?
themes.approach: I work on quantum optimal control with pulses; deep reinforcement learning for optimal pulse shaping in single-photon quantum emitters; reinforcement-learning-based NISQ state preparation; analytical design of an LC double-notch Purcell filter for superconducting circuits; and quantum reservoir learning for reinforcement-learning-optimized pulse and Hamiltonian control of a Rydberg lattice.

themes.title: Quantum Machine Learning
themes.tagline: Learning-based characterisation of quantum states, and hybrid quantum–classical models.
themes.problem: Near-term devices produce noisy, high-dimensional quantum data that is costly to characterise, and parameterised quantum circuits are only useful if they can be embedded in learning pipelines and understood. How can learned models classify and discriminate quantum states that matter for metrology? Where do variational circuits fit in hybrid models, and which design choices (data encoding, entangling gates, circuit depth) shape what the model learns?
themes.approach: I work on deep neural networks for multiclass classification of metrologically resourceful tripartite states; neural networks built from variational quantum circuits; hybrid quantum–classical vision models; quantum-assisted reinforcement learning; and a survey of quantum machine learning for drug discovery. In the 2025 IonQ Summer Research Mentoring Program I studied explainability of quantum machine learning models.

themes.title: Variational Algorithms & Optimization
themes.tagline: Mapping network and transport scheduling problems onto variational quantum circuits.
themes.problem: Scheduling and routing in communication and transport networks are NP-hard, and real instances are large. Can they be written as QUBO or Hamiltonian problems that variational algorithms solve on today's IBM Quantum backends, and what do hybrid quantum–classical solvers offer for edge intelligence and resource allocation?
themes.approach: I work on the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) for network scheduling using a QUBO formulation; VQE-based traffic routing and EV charging scheduling for intelligent transportation systems; and variational circuits for hybrid optimization. I was principal investigator on two Brain Korea 21 projects in this area.

themes.title: Error Mitigation & NISQ Computing
themes.tagline: Cheap, adaptive mitigation of readout and measurement errors on noisy devices.
themes.problem: Noise caps what NISQ devices can do. Full tomography is too expensive to repeat as devices drift, so can measurement and readout errors be mitigated adaptively, with learned models that transfer across devices and over time?
themes.approach: I work on measurement error mitigation for NISQ devices; adaptive quantum readout error mitigation with transfer learning; and machine-learning-based qubit state estimation on IBM Quantum hardware.
